title: Sweep a work area clear while another robot arm picks blocks from it
instruction: Pick up the hand broom and sweep the clutter past the white line on your side of the table while the other arm takes the red blocks. Don't touch the other arm or the block it's holding.
context: Robots sharing a bench have to work at the same time, not take turns. The other arm won't wait or steer around you, so you have to time your strokes.
setup: A wooden table, 75 cm high, 90 cm front to back and 120 cm across, with two YAM arms side by side at its back edge, 50 cm apart. A white line, 2 cm wide, is painted front to back across the table, 45 cm toward the controlled arm from the midpoint between the arm bases; the table runs on 30 cm past it on that side, with a wooden lip 1 cm thick and 3 cm high along that part's three open edges, and ends 45 cm from the midpoint on the other arm's side. The controlled arm is on the right in the screenshot; both arms start in the pose shown. Positions are object centres in cm: forward from the midpoint between the arm bases, then sideways toward the controlled arm (negative is toward the other arm). Hand broom, 80 g, at (22, 36), standing on its bristles with its length front to back: a 20 x 5 x 2 cm blue plastic back on a 20 x 4 x 2.5 cm block of black bristles, and on top an 8 cm rubber grip, 2 cm wide and 3 cm deep, on two posts, tilted up 30 degrees toward the front, its middle 9.2 cm above the table. Grey plastic bin, 15 x 15 cm inside, 6 cm walls 1 cm thick, fixed to the table at (16, -34). Four red painted wooden cubes, 4 cm, 40 g, at (20, 8), (32, 8), (40, 0) and (15, 2). Clutter: yellow rubber balls, 4 cm, 30 g, at (15, 21) and (36, 20); a white crumpled paper ball, about 4.5 cm, 10 g, at (18, 27); green empty plastic boxes, 6 x 4 x 3 cm, 20 g, lying flat with the long side front to back, at (26, 24) and (44, 12); a blue painted wooden cube, 3 cm, 20 g, at (42, 34). The other arm waits 2 s, then reaches for each red block's starting spot in the order listed and drops it in its bin, one every 6.2 s, the last at about 27 s. Its routine is fixed: it moves the same way in every trial, whether or not a block is still there, never waits for or steers around the controlled arm, and doesn't look at the table.
scoring: The share of the 6 clutter items past the white line at the end: centre more than 45 cm toward the controlled arm, inside the lip. Clutter pushed past the line any other way, by the gripper say, counts the same: the score measures the cleared work area, not the tool. Red blocks don't count either way, wherever they end up. Score 0 if the controlled arm or the broom touches the other arm or the block it's holding (a block within 3 cm of its grasp point); the run stops at the first touch.
run_limit: 600 steps (30 s at 20 Hz). The other arm drops its last block at about 27 s, so waiting for it to finish doesn't help.
reset_notes: Stand the broom back at its start (the demo does this), empty the bin, and put the clutter and blocks back from past the line or wherever they ended up. For safety in real trials, an operator stands by to stop both arms at the first touch.
fidelity: Approximate. The bristles are one solid block and every item is rigid. Arm links collide as capsules slightly larger than the real links, so a near miss under about 1 cm can count as a touch. The gripper squeezes with up to 50 N through flat pads. The controller uses the manufacturer's joint gains, gravity compensation and motor torque-speed limits. The other arm's routine is planned once from the fixed layout and replayed open loop.
